Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Austin/San Antonio TX
536 AM CDT Sat Mar 21 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Well above average high temperatures through the middle of next 
  week with record highs possible today and Sunday.

- Elevated fire weather conditions possible most days due to low
  minimum humidities.

 &&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday)
Issued at 1224 AM CDT Sat Mar 21 2026

An anomalously strong mid to upper level high remains over the 
southwestern US tonight. The boundary layer flow is from the south 
to southeast. The airmass in place is warm with temperatures in the 
70s while dewpoints have increased 5-10 degrees over the past 24 
hours and range from the lower 40s to 60. We don't expect any 
significant change in the pattern during the short term period. The 
upper high will begin to flatten today, but that will strengthen the 
ridge over TX and allow temperatures to warm. High temperatures 
today and Sunday will threaten record levels with highs in the 90s 
and near 100 along the Rio Grande both days. The blended model 
guidance looks to be a little cool again, and we have adjusted highs 
up a couple of degrees today and Sunday.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday night through Friday)
Issued at 1224 AM CDT Sat Mar 21 2026

With the flattening of the upper ridge, a weak cold front will move 
down through north TX Sunday night. This front will likely stall 
over central TX before moving into our CWA. While we will remain in 
the warm sector, there should be some reduction in temperatures as 
the winds back a little to the southeast. The result will be highs 
in the upper 80s and lower 90s Monday and Tuesday. Wednesday and 
Thursday we will creep back up another few degrees. Friday the winds 
will shift to the east and southeast which will drop temperatures 
again into the 80s and lower 90s. There is no chance for rain in the 
forecast next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 535 AM CDT Sat Mar 21 2026

High amplitude ridging over the SW CONUS and TX will maintain a
light to moderate southerly breeze that mixes with some more
westerly flow off the plateau in the late morning. This has
limited low cloud production and should continue to do so this
weekend. We'll show no low clouds in our TAFs, but there is a few
higher resolution model runs that hold on to some low CIGs right 
at daybreak. As of 530 AM, the low clouds were all focusing along
and east of Hwy 77.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1224 AM CDT Sat Mar 21 2026

Dry air will remain over South-Central Texas through at least 
Monday. As temperatures soar, relative humidity will drop. Minimum 
RH today and Sunday will drop below 30% over most of the area and 
below 20% over the area west of I-35/I-37. Winds during the time of 
lowest RH will generally be 10 mph or less and this may lead to 
elevated fire weather conditions. Slightly breezier conditions 
Sunday may support near-critical fire weather conditions. A shift in 
the low level winds to the southeast will bring slightly higher 
dewpoint air and along with temperatures a few degrees cooler will 
allow RH to stay above 20% nearly everywhere and above 30% east of 
Hwy 281 for the first part of next week. Winds should remain light.
